fluff.overview: The Enyo Strike Tank is a fifty-five ton tracked combat vehicle designed by Clan Hell's Horses to exploit the advantages of lightweight engine technology in a production battle tank. Commissioned by Khan Malavai Fletcher as a fast, hard-hitting cavalry support platform capable of keeping pace with medium BattleMechs, the Enyo filled a gap in the Horses' touman for a purpose-built strike tank in the medium weight class. Lighter and faster than the Clan's existing armor assets, the design was intended specifically for use in Cavalry and Strike Cluster formations where speed and maneuverability were prized over raw firepower. Entering production in 3063, the Enyo quickly proved its value and has since been manufactured at multiple facilities, spawning several production variants that reflect the Horses' continued commitment to vehicle-centric combined-arms warfare.
fluff.capabilities:
Powered by a Type 330 extralight fusion engine, the Enyo can reach a top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, fast enough to keep pace with most Clan medium BattleMechs. The extralight engine's compact profile frees significant internal volume for weapons and ammunition while keeping the vehicle at a manageable weight. Seven and a half tons of Compound VM20 ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection for the tank's weight class, supplemented by CASE in the ammunition bays to mitigate the risk of catastrophic ammunition explosions.

The primary armament is a Series 44h large pulse laser mounted in the turret, offering excellent accuracy and unlimited ammunition. Three Type VI-Bravo Streak SRM-6 launchers provide devastating short-range firepower, with each launcher fed by its own dedicated ammunition bin for respectable endurance. One launcher is turret-mounted alongside the laser, while the other two face forward. A pair of Series IX machine guns, one on each flank, offer protection against unarmored infantry. The Enyo's main limitation is its reliance on speed over heavy armor thickness, as prolonged engagements against heavier opponents can quickly overwhelm its protective envelope.
fluff.deployment: Developed in 3075 alongside the Horses' broader effort to expand vehicle production at Kirchbach, the Sholef variant takes a markedly different tactical approach than the standard Enyo. The turret houses an LB 10-X autocannon capable of firing both solid and cluster ammunition, a plasma cannon for area denial and heat generation, and an SRM-6 launcher. Two additional forward-mounted SRM-6 launchers and a pair of anti-personnel Gauss rifles round out the armament, giving the Sholef considerable versatility across engagement types. An ECM suite provides electronic warfare capability unusual for a vehicle of this class. The Sholef serves primarily in Hell's Horses formations operating in the former Wolf occupation zone, where its flexible loadout suits the varied combat conditions encountered along contested borders.
fluff.history:
The Enyo's development traces directly to Clan Hell's Horses' tradition of integrating combat vehicles into their touman alongside BattleMechs. Khan Malavai Fletcher initiated the project after observing the success of XL-engine refits on the Mars assault vehicle, envisioning a purpose-built strike tank that could serve as a lighter, faster complement to the Horses' existing armor assets. Fletcher directed his scientists to develop a production battle tank in the medium weight class capable of outmaneuvering most Clan-built armor units while keeping pace with supporting BattleMech forces.

Fletcher's disastrous campaign against the Ghost Bears led to the ejection of the Horses from the Inner Sphere and his subsequent removal by Khan James Cobb. Though these circumstances could have ended the Enyo project, Cobb recognized the soundness of Fletcher's designs and allowed development to continue. Full production began in 3063 at Kirin Armory Plant 4, the Horses' primary armored vehicle facility in the Clan Homeworlds.

As the Hell's Horses prepared for their relocation to the Inner Sphere, production on Kirin ceased when the world was traded to Clan Coyote during the Wars of Reaving after 3070. The Horses reestablished Enyo production at the upgraded Swedenborg Heavy Industries facilities on Kirchbach, which had been captured from Clan Wolf. Swedenborg had originally been an IndustrialMech manufacturer under Combine and later Free Rasalhague Republic control before the Wolf Clan seized the world during the Clan Invasion. Under Hell's Horses ownership, the site was expanded with new production lines for vehicles, battle armor, and various components. By 3079, the facility was operating at ninety-five percent capacity. The Kirchbach plant also became the production site for the Sholef and ER Pulse variants, while the experimental XR prototype was developed separately at Provisional Testing Site Stallion on Nouveaux Paris, with only four units completed before resource constraints halted the program.
